rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a full/expanded blastocyst with strong ICM and sparse poor-quality TE, matching the reported AC pattern and image overall. Minor issue: it calls the embryo 'high-grade/good-quality,' which overstates a C-grade TE embryo, and it notes some features not confidently assessable from a single frame.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, prior biochemical pregnancies, tubal factor/hydrosalpinx concern, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrium, and ovarian response with embryo morphology and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, especially around age-related aneuploidy limiting prognosis despite decent morphology. Small inconsistency in describing the embryo as 'high-grade/good-quality' while also emphasizing C-grade TE and very low implantation odds.

Generally consistent with IVF practice and Gardner grading concepts, including emphasis on age-related euploidy decline, SET, uterine cavity review, and hydrosalpinx management. Slight overstatement of PGT-A benefits and some wording around grading quality could be more guideline-nuanced.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, cavity/hydrosalpinx assessment, luteal support considerations, reserve testing, PGT-A discussion, and selective recurrent loss workup.
